newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish up, buoyed by Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish up, buoyed by Greenspan.

text.p: French stocks turned positive during the last half hour of trading and finished higher on Tuesday after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 3.78 points, or 0.16 percent, at 2,409.88 after recovering from a session low of 2,384.77. The CAC-40 January futures contract rose three points to 2,415. Volume was 6.3 billion francs.
"Greenspan reassured the markets with his comments. Wall Street went up and so did we," one trader said. "But you have to be careful when you remember the impact he had last time."
Greenspan said U.S. inflation was rising more slowing and economic growth rising faster than official data suggest.
He described the rise in the U.S. stock market as "breathtaking" but the comment appeared more neutral than his market-moving remarks in the fall that the euphoria might be overdone.

* Shares in luxury goods group LVMH closed down 0.74 percent at 1,484 francs on profit-taking. Lehman Brothers downgraded the stock to underperform but many analysts remain bullish on LVMH and applaud its recent purchase of DFS and sale of Guinness shares.

* Shares in catering group Sodexho fell 4.46 percent to 2,675 francs after Cheuvreux de Virieu dropped the stock from its favoured list. Fund managers said Cheuvreux remained positive on the stock but felt it was overpriced.

* Eurotunnel rose 6.85 percent to 7.80 francs, extending Monday's 5.8 percent gain, after reporting higher 1996 revenues and prospects for the finalisation by March of the details of a bank debt accord.
* A Sofres poll published in the newspaper La Tribune found 58 percent of market operators believe the bourse has potential to keep rising from current near-record levels.

* Pernod Ricard rose 3.68 percent to 310 francs. It said its SEGM unit had signed an agreement to take control of Greek company EPOM, the country's second biggest producer of ouzo with its Mini brand.
